purpose: Calcipotriene is used to treat plaque psoriasis, a skin condition that causes thick, scaly, red patches on the skin. It helps slow down the overgrowth of skin cells that causes those rough, flaky patches. It can be used on the body or scalp depending on the form your doctor prescribes.
how_it_works: Your skin cells in psoriasis grow way too fast, which causes those thick, scaly buildup patches. Calcipotriene is a man-made form of Vitamin D that tells your skin cells to slow down and grow at a more normal pace. It also helps reduce some of the redness and inflammation in the affected areas.
common_side_effects: Burning, itching, or stinging where you apply it. Skin irritation, dryness, peeling, or redness. Occasionally a rash around the treated area. These effects are usually mild and often improve as your skin adjusts.
warnings: Do not use this on your face, groin, or underarms unless your doctor specifically tells you to, as it can cause extra irritation in those sensitive areas. Using too much or covering too large an area of skin can raise your calcium levels in the blood, which can cause symptoms like nausea, weakness, or confusion — so only use the amount your doctor prescribed. Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems or a history of high calcium levels, as this medication may not be right for you. Avoid getting it in your eyes.
typical_dosing: Most adults apply a thin layer to the affected skin areas once or twice a day, depending on the form prescribed. Your doctor will tell you exactly how much to use and how often. Do not use more than the recommended amount per week, as using too much can cause side effects throughout your whole body.
